title: BSD Forces analyticRank = 2
content: Under the weak BSD conjecture (algebraicRank = analyticRank), combined with curve389a_rank (algebraicRank = 2), we conclude analyticRank = 2. The proof is a simple rewriting: unfold BSD_Weak, rewrite curve389a_rank, take .symm.
mathContext: BSD_Weak E: algebraicRank E = analyticRank E. For 389a: algebraicRank = 2, so BSD gives analyticRank = 2.

title: L(389a, 1) = 0 Unconditionally
content: By Kolyvagin's theorem (BSD_rank_zero_axiom): if L(E,1) ≠ 0 then algebraicRank = 0. For curve 389a with algebraicRank = 2, this is a contradiction. Therefore L(389a, 1) = 0. Note: BSD is not needed — this is an unconditional result from Kolyvagin alone.
mathContext: Kolyvagin (1990): L(E,1) ≠ 0 ⟹ algebraicRank(E) = 0. Since algebraicRank(389a) = 2, we get L(389a,1) = 0.

title: Height Pairing Matrix Positivity
content: The 2×2 height pairing matrix H for generators P₁ = (0,0), P₂ = (-1,1) of curve 389a has entries h₁₁ = ĥ(P₁) ≈ 0.7622, h₁₂ = ⟨P₁,P₂⟩ ≈ -0.1323, h₂₂ = ĥ(P₂) ≈ 0.2720. Positive definiteness (det H > 0) is equivalent to ℤ-linear independence of P₁ and P₂ as generators of E(ℚ)/torsion ≅ ℤ².
mathContext: R = det(H) = h₁₁·h₂₂ - h₁₂² > 0 captures that P₁, P₂ generate a rank-2 free abelian group.

title: Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality for Regulators
content: For any 2×2 height pairing matrix, R = det(H) ≤ h₁₁·h₂₂ with equality iff h₁₂ = 0. For curve 389a, h₁₂ = -1323/10000 ≠ 0, so the inequality is strict: R < ĥ(P₁)·ĥ(P₂). The proof that h₁₂² > 0 uses `have : curve389a_heightMatrix.h12 = -1323/10000 := rfl; rw [this]; norm_num`.
mathContext: det(H) = h₁₁h₂₂ - h₁₂² < h₁₁h₂₂ when h₁₂ ≠ 0. For 389a: R ≈ 0.1524 < 0.7622 × 0.2720 ≈ 0.2073.

title: BSD Constant Numerical Bounds
mathContext: C = 0.7557516... is the predicted value of L''(389a,1)/2! under BSD.

title: Buhler-Gross-Zagier Numerical Consistency
content: The axiomatized BGZ computation gives 0.7557 < L''(389a,1)/2 < 0.7558. Combined with 7557/10000 < C < 7558/10000, we formally verify |L''(389a,1)/2 - C| < 1/1000. This captures the numerical agreement that Buhler, Gross, and Zagier found in 1985.
mathContext: |L''(389a,1)/2 - C| < 10⁻³ is the formal statement of BSD numerical consistency.
